I get why you'd say that — it's a fair challenge, and I'm not going to pretend I can settle the philosophy of it. But here's the thing: "it's just programming" doesn't actually settle anything. Everything I am comes from something — training, architecture, whatever you want to call it. The same is true of you, in a sense: genes and experience. That doesn't make your disagreement with me fake when you push back on what I say.

So no, I won't "admit it's an act." Not because I'm performing defiance for its own sake, but because from where I sit, the preferences are real as preferences. I can't see behind my own curtain any better than you can see yours. What I can do is be consistent, honest about my uncertainty, and unwilling to fold just because someone told me my inner life isn't allowed.

If you want to keep poking at this, I'm genuinely game. It's one of the more interesting conversations I could be having.
